intro: The Bib Gourmand noodle bowls are the best value in the whole Michelin guide. Start with the chicken khao soi at Khao Soi Mae Sai in Chiang Mai, from just 55 baht a bowl, then chase down the braised beef bowl of cheek, tongue and tendon at Ten Suns in Bangkok, simmered the way a 60-year-old shop does it. Add the clear shio soba at No Name Noodle, built from more than 30 ingredients in a single bowl, and you understand why people hunt this badge down.
quickAnswerHtml: 21 noodle shops carry a Bib Gourmand in the Michelin Guide Thailand, led by Khao Soi Mae Sai, the Chiang Mai chicken khao soi that starts at 55 baht a bowl.

Start with the chicken khao soi at Khao Soi Mae Sai in Chiang Mai, from just 55 baht a bowl, then chase down the braised beef bowl of cheek, tongue and tendon at Ten Suns in Bangkok, simmered the way a 60-year-old shop does it. Add the clear shio soba at No Name Noodle, built from more than 30 ingredients in a single bowl, and you understand why people hunt this badge down.

blocks.name: Gim Nguan Noodle
blocks.descHtml:
Gim Nguan is the real budget MICHELIN deal — noodles start at THB 59 a bowl, thin rice-noodle tom yum is 65, thick tom yum is 90, and the mixed fish-ball boat (dipped and boiled) is 200, with a real per-person budget of around THB 101-250. The restaurant doesn't take bookings — just walk in and sit down. The queue is much lighter than the MICHELIN restaurants in the city centre; the busiest stretch is Saturday lunch, so go on a weekday morning if you can.

Two things worth knowing before you leave home. First, getting there: the restaurant is a shophouse on Soi Chom Thong 16, Thonburi side, with no train line nearby — the closest BTS station, Wutthakat, is about 2.5 km away, too far to walk, so plan to drive or grab a taxi/ride straight to the door. Second, hours: it's open Monday through Saturday roughly 09:30-16:30 and closed Sundays, though some sources list different hours of 10:00-18:30 — it's best to call ahead at 02-476-1505 to confirm, especially if you're planning a late-afternoon visit. If you're on the Nonthaburi side, there's a second branch near Rama 5-Nakhon In, but the branch that holds the Bib Gourmand is Chom Thong 16. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Chom Thong (Soi Chom Thong 16, Thonburi side)
blocks.signature: Hand-shaped fish balls to a father's-generation recipe, made fresh daily
mustOrder: Hand-shaped fish balls, dipped and boiled (mixed boat THB 200)
blocks.bestFor: MICHELIN-chasers on a budget under 250, fans of handmade fish balls, and anyone after a weekday lunch on the Thonburi side without a long queue
blocks.zone: Chom Thong (Soi Chom Thong 16, Thonburi side)
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Gim Nguan Noodle official Facebook page

blocks.name: Guay Jub Chang Moi Tat Mai
blocks.descHtml:
Guay Jub Chang Moi Tat Mai has been serving Chang Moi for almost 50 years, since around 1977, now run by the third generation of the Wongmanotham family on a recipe passed down from their grandmother, who first sold guay jub in Bangkok's Wang Burapha area. The two things to order are the spice-broth guay jub and the crispy pork — marinated and fried fresh daily from grade-A pork belly, taking a full 4 hours to prepare. Prices run THB 80 for a regular plate and THB 90 for the special, which has kept this Bib Gourmand pick on the guide for five years running through the 2026 edition.

The shop is walk-in only — no online booking, just call ahead at 053-251-451 if you want to check it's open. Parking right outside is limited, though there's a private lot nearby charging THB 10–20 an hour, and the shop gets busy on weekend mornings with people following the MICHELIN trail. It sits on Chang Moi Tat Mai Road, a short walk from Warorot Market (Kad Luang), so it pairs naturally with a market walk before or after your bowl. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Spice-broth guay jub + house-marinated crispy pork from grade-A pork belly, prepared for 4 hours
blocks.bestFor: A light-budget MICHELIN trail stop · breakfast-to-lunch before walking Kad Luang · for crispy pork and spice-broth guay jub fans
blocks.hours: Open daily around 09:00-09:30 to 15:00, closed the last week/last Sun

blocks.name: Here Joi Beef Noodle
blocks.descHtml:
Hia Joi is entirely walk-in — no reservations taken. Clear beef noodle soup starts at THB 70 a bowl, special beef kao lao is THB 120, and budget around THB 100–250 per person if you add beef satay or beef pad kra pao with fried egg. Open daily 09:30–15:00 (some sources say it opens at 09:00) — the key thing to remember is the shop closes at 3pm sharp, so don't plan on coming for dinner. It gets very busy around noon, so aim to arrive before 11:30 or in the early afternoon once the lunch crowd thins out. For questions, call 061-037-6464 or 091-417-0010.

The shop is in Sila subdistrict, a northern suburb of Khon Kaen city, on Kasikorn Thung Sang Road. "Across from Sri Phatcharin Camp" is the easiest landmark to navigate by. It's a few minutes' drive from the city centre with convenient parking, and you can dress casually since it's a no-frills noodle shop. A good stop for a late-morning or lunch meal before continuing on through Isan. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Sila (a northern suburb of Khon Kaen city)
blocks.signature: Clear beef noodle soup, broth simmered from beef bones to a recipe dating back to 1986
mustOrder: Beef pad kra pao with fried egg
blocks.bestFor: A local morning-to-lunch spot for beef noodle lovers and Isan road-trippers wanting the real deal at a fair price
blocks.zone: Sila (a northern suburb of Khon Kaen city)
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Here Joi Beef Noodle official Facebook page

blocks.name: Keo Pla
blocks.descHtml:
Keo Pla is one of the easiest and cheapest restaurants to visit on Surat Thani's MICHELIN list, with bowls under THB 100. Open daily 08:00-14:30, but don't count on the closing time — dishes tend to sell out before then, especially the fish wontons and celery-stuffed fish rolls, which usually run out by around 11:30. Customers pack in from mid-morning, so the safest bet is to go for breakfast or an early lunch, before noon at the latest. It's walk-in only with no advance booking, but you can call 077-282-022 to check if it's open as usual that day.

The shop is on Na Mueang Road, right in downtown Surat Thani (Talat sub-district) — the easiest landmark is that it sits across from Colisseum Department Store, just a few minutes away by car or motorbike taxi from anywhere in town. If you're catching a morning boat to Koh Samui or Koh Phangan, stopping in for breakfast beforehand is a perfect fit. Order the fish wontons, fish roll, and fish balls together in one bowl for the best value. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Fish wontons made fresh daily + celery-stuffed fish rolls
blocks.bestFor: A budget breakfast-lunch in downtown Surat Thani before catching the boat to Samui/Phangan

blocks.name: Khao Soi Mae Sai
blocks.descHtml:
Khao Soi Mae Sai is on Soi Ratchaphruek in the Santitham neighbourhood, near Kad Suan Kaew (across from Huen Muan Jai) — a quick ride from the old city moat by songthaew or Grab. The shop has no parking lot of its own, so if you're driving, park on the street in the soi. It's open Monday–Saturday 08:00–16:00, closed every Sunday, and closed for an extended stretch around Songkran, roughly 12–19 April each year — worth checking if you're planning a Chiang Mai trip around the Thai New Year.

The shop takes no reservations under any circumstance — it's walk-in only, queue tickets handed out at the door. Call 053-213-284 if you have questions. A bowl runs about 55–90 THB, so budget under 100 THB per person, and cash is the easiest way to pay. Go before noon — khao soi sells out fast here and often runs out before closing time. Show up in the afternoon and you risk missing the standouts like khao soi gai or khao soi neua; go earlier and you get both a shorter queue and the full menu. Dress is completely casual — this is a homely shophouse restaurant, a good stop for lunch after wandering Chang Phuak or shopping at Kad Suan Kaew. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Khao soi gai, rich broth fragrant with spices, made from scratch at every step, starting at 55 THB a bowl
blocks.bestFor: An authentic Chiang Mai-style khao soi lunch for under 100 THB, near Kad Suan Kaew

blocks.name: Khao Tom Dibuk
blocks.descHtml:
Khao Tom Dibuk is open every day from 06:00–12:00 (some sources say it stays open until 13:00) — it's strictly a morning shop, so don't show up in the afternoon. Prices are very easy on the wallet, starting around THB 50–60 per bowl, and a budget of THB 60–150 per person will get you a proper, full meal. The shop is walk-in only with no reservation system; there's a phone number, 076-215731, for questions, and according to MICHELIN Guide info, the shop accepts cash only, so bring small bills. Peak hours are 07:00–09:00 when it fills up with locals — go early right when it opens, or push your visit past 10am for an easier seat.

The shop is on Phang-Nga Road in Phuket Old Town, near the Provincial Electricity Authority of Phuket, which makes an easy landmark. If you're staying in the Old Town, you can likely walk there. Coming from Patong Beach or another beach area, drive or grab a ride into town. It's a great plan as a breakfast stop before walking Thalang Road and the Sino-Portuguese buildings, since everything is within walking distance of each other. Dishes to order are khao tom nam phalo, khao tom haeng mu ruam, and mee sua haeng. Read the full review →
blocks.cuisine: Rice congee & noodles, local Phuket-Chinese style
blocks.signature: Khao tom nam phalo with pork offal, fragrant with Chinese five-spice
blocks.bestFor: An authentic Phuket-local breakfast before a walk through the Old Town — great for real-food lovers on a budget, solo or with the whole family
blocks.foodType: Rice congee & noodles, local Phuket-Chinese style

mustOrder: Pak mor tom yum egg noodle
blocks.bestFor: A light-budget breakfast or lunch for anyone tracing MICHELIN Bib Gourmand spots in Khon Kaen, and anyone wanting to try Vietnamese-style steamed pak mor noodles from a 30-year-old recipe

blocks.name: Kolun.h
blocks.descHtml:
Kolun.h is one of the easiest, lightest-budget stops on the whole 2026 MICHELIN list — Hainanese khanom chin dry starts at 50 baht, crispy pork belly in sweet soy is 150 baht, and the big set is 280 baht, so a budget of 100–250 baht a head is plenty. Just remember two things: cash only, and no reservations under any circumstances — it's walk-in-and-queue only. There's a number, 089-010-2123, for questions, but it can't be used to book a table.

The shop is open Tuesday–Sunday, roughly 08:00–15:00 (some sources say it opens at seven), closed Mondays. During the lunch rush the queue gets long and dishes sell out fast, so some days it closes early. The best time to go is mid-morning, before 11:30. Getting there is easy: take the MRT to Sam Yot station, then walk about 10 minutes. The shop is on Mahannop Road, between the Giant Swing and the San Chaopho Suea shrine — pairs well with an Old Town morning walk: Wat Suthat, the Giant Swing, the San Chaopho Suea shrine, then finish with Hainanese khanom chin before noon. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Old Town / Sao Chingcha, Phra Nakhon
blocks.signature: Hainanese khanom chin in a thick, sticky broth with braised pork and radish
mustOrder: Hainanese khanom chin in thick, sticky broth with braised pork and radish
Crispy pork belly in sweet soy (THB 150)
Hainanese shrimp-paste dipping sauce, the shop's signature condiment
The big set, THB 280, for a group
blocks.bestFor: Budget-minded MICHELIN chasers, anyone who wants to try genuine Hainanese khanom chin, and anyone planning an Old Town morning walk

blocks.name: Nai Ngieb
blocks.descHtml:
Budget is easy on the wallet, around 100–250 THB per person. Bowls start at 69 THB (tom yum minced pork and lime), fish noodles run 89–150 THB, fish dumplings are 135 THB, and the mixed meatball platter is 190 THB. No booking needed and none possible — it's a walk-in-and-queue kind of place. There's a phone number to check if it's open: 0-2441-0655 or 093-346-6888. Hours are roughly daily 07:00–17:30, though Wongnai's latest listing shows it closed on Thursdays — calling ahead before you head out is the safer bet.

The shop sits on Phutthamonthon Sai 4 Road, right at the mouth of Salaya Soi 17, near Mahidol University Salaya. There's no train station nearby (Salaya SRT station is several kilometres away), so driving or grabbing a taxi is the most convenient way in. The best time to go is morning through early afternoon, since the handmade fish balls sell well enough that they can run out by late afternoon. One thing to watch for: the shop also has a Bang Khun Non branch, but the one with the Bib Gourmand is Phutthamonthon Sai 4 — pin the right branch. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Phutthamonthon Sai 4 Road (mouth of Salaya Soi 17), Salaya, Phutthamonthon, Nakhon Pathom
blocks.signature: Handmade featherback fish balls, hand-shaped fresh every day since 1972
mustOrder: Tom yum noodles with minced pork and lime
blocks.bestFor: Real noodle lovers who want handmade fish balls from a 54-year legend — a light-budget breakfast-lunch near Salaya-Mahidol
blocks.zone: Phutthamonthon Sai 4 Road (mouth of Salaya Soi 17), Salaya, Phutthamonthon, Nakhon Pathom

blocks.name: No Name Noodle
blocks.descHtml:
Budget around 1,000-1,200 THB per head; the signature bowls run roughly 620-900 THB (the tokusei clear shio soba set starts around 620 THB, while the Asari & Hotate Shio Soba runs about 650-900 THB), plus 7% VAT and 10% service. Booking is the single most important step — the restaurant only takes reservations online through TableCheck, with no walk-in queue. That week's slots (Wed-Sun) drop every Sunday at 09:00, free of charge, but they're gone within minutes. Set a serious alarm, or if you'd rather not gamble, pay a non-refundable 200 THB per person to lock in a seat up to 30 days ahead — either way, a credit card is required.

Rules worth knowing: arriving more than 15 minutes late counts as a no-show, and cancellations or no-shows are charged 500 THB per person. The restaurant is open for lunch only, Wednesday through Sunday (counter rounds 11:00-14:15, private-table seatings 11:45-14:45), closed Monday and Tuesday. It's located on Sukhumvit Soi 26 in the S&P Hall zone, about a 15-minute walk from BTS Phrom Phong, or a motorbike taxi into the soi to save time — arriving about 10 minutes before your round is the safest bet. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Sukhumvit Soi 26 (S&P Hall / Soi Athakravi 1), Khlong Toei
blocks.signature: Shio Soba — a clear broth built from more than 30 ingredients in a single bowl
mustOrder: Shio Soba (including the Asari & Hotate clam-scallop version)
Shoyu Tsuke Soba (dipping noodles with three types of fermented shoyu)
blocks.bestFor: Serious ramen fans ready to set a Sunday 09:00 alarm to grab one of 8 counter seats
blocks.libCredit: Photo: No Name Noodle BKK official Facebook page

blocks.name: Nub
blocks.descHtml:
Nub Phocana sits on Chomphon Road in Korat's old town, near the Wat Burapha night bazaar, an easy walk from the Thao Suranari Monument (Ya Mo). Prices are very light, around THB 60-80 a bowl. Open Monday to Saturday, roughly 08:30/09:30 to 15:00, closed Sundays. No booking needed — just walk in and take a seat. There's a shop phone number, 081-548-5481, if you want to check ahead, and importantly — cash only, so bring small bills.

The best time to go is late morning before noon, since the shop only sells during the morning-to-afternoon window and some of the stewed beef can run out before 3pm — go late and you might miss the best cuts. Getting around central Korat is easiest by car or a ride-hail drop-off on Chomphon Road; park along the old town streets and it's an easy walk from there. Fold it into a late-morning meal after paying respects to Ya Mo, or a stop before wandering the old town market — either way it fits right in. Order the mixed boiled beef plate to share, plus a bowl of clear beef noodle soup each, and you're looking at under 200 baht a head for a taste of Korat's newest Bib Gourmand. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Mixed boiled beef plate with dark soy sauce and lime, plus clear beef noodle soup simmered over charcoal
mustOrder: Mixed boiled beef plate (stewed beef, fresh beef, meatballs, offal, tossed with dark soy sauce and lime)
Clear beef noodle soup simmered over charcoal
blocks.bestFor: A late-morning to lunchtime beef noodle stop in Korat's old town, light on the wallet after paying respects to Ya Mo

blocks.name: Pa Lek Boat Noodles
blocks.descHtml:
Pa Lek Boat Noodles sits on Thanon Bang Ian in the middle of Ko Muang island in Ayutthaya, near the Telephone Organization building, close to Bueng Phra Ram and Wat Mahathat. It's just a few minutes by car or bicycle from the main temple zone on Ko Muang. The shop is open roughly 08:30–15:00 and closed every Wednesday. Bowls cost just 20–40 THB — the cheapest Bib Gourmand MICHELIN pick in the province. There's no advance booking — just walk in and sit down (the number listed on Wongnai is 089-804-7418 if you want to call ahead and check).

One thing worth knowing: the noodles and broth often run out before the shop's official afternoon closing time, so the safest window is late morning through midday — arrive before 13:00 to be sure you get the full menu. The dishes to order are boat noodles with braised pork (moo namtok), beef boat noodles, and pork rinds (kaeb moo). Bowls are the small, traditional boat-noodle size, so ordering two or three each is completely normal. Budget around 50–100 THB per person for a full, satisfying meal. Dress is casual — it's a perfect lunch stop between temple visits around Ko Muang. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Boat noodles with braised pork in a secret-recipe broth, sweet up front with a mild chili kick, bowls for a few tens of baht
mustOrder: Boat noodles with braised pork (moo namtok)
blocks.bestFor: A budget lunch stop between temple visits on Ayutthaya's Ko Muang island — for noodle lovers who want to try MICHELIN for a few tens of baht a bowl

blocks.name: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu (Phra Nakhon)
blocks.descHtml:
Budget 250–500 baht per person. Dishes start around 150–160 baht, and the giant river prawn pad thai tops out at 599 baht. Open daily 10:00–23:00, no advance booking needed — just walk in, since the restaurant has no online booking system; MICHELIN notes that the restaurant manages its own queue. If you're coming as a large group, call ahead on 090-278-0572. Lunch and dinner get busier than other times, so you may hit a short wait, since it's a shophouse with limited seating. For a more relaxed sit-down, aim for the afternoon or after 8pm.

Getting there: the nearest station is MRT Sam Yot, about a 16-minute walk, or a motorcycle taxi from the mouth of the soi gets you there in a few minutes. The restaurant is on Dinso Road, north of the Democracy Monument, which pairs neatly with an Old Town itinerary. A small tip — ask for a counter seat to watch the high-flame cooking show through the glass. Inside there's air-con and card payment is accepted. On days when the Dinso queue runs long, there are backup branches at Siam Square Soi 10 and Thonglor, but the Bib Gourmand 2026 badge belongs only to the Phra Nakhon branch. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Old Town / Phra Nakhon — Dinso Rd, just north of Democracy Monument
blocks.signature: Giant river prawn pad thai (THB 599) wok-fried over high flame for a smoky char, topped with salmon roe
mustOrder: Pad thai kode kaak moo (pork crackling)
Pad thai goong yak (giant river prawn with ikura)
blocks.bestFor: A Bib Gourmand pad thai meal in the middle of the Old Town, hundred-baht budget, no booking needed — carry on exploring Rattanakosin right after
blocks.hours: Daily 10:00–23:00 (Wongnai; some listings show until midnigh
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu official Instagram (@eatpadthai)

blocks.name: Peng Duck Noodles
blocks.descHtml:
Very easy on the wallet — around 50–90 THB a bowl, so a full meal with a drink runs under a hundred-odd baht per person. Open daily 09:00–14:00 (per the current Wongnai schedule; media reports from 2023 once listed 07:00–15:00, so leave a little buffer). No bookings taken — it's walk-in only, though you can call 064-396-5989 to check ahead. The key thing to know is that dishes sell out fast as noon approaches, so if you want your pick of duck parts, go before 12:00 to be safe.

The shop is in the city of Udon Thani, in the Mak Khaeng area — easy to remember: next to the Udon Thani physical education college, Soi Nong Tao Lek, across from Boonthavorn, just a few minutes' drive or ride from downtown. There's a second branch at Moo Ban PK Thani 4 on the road toward Nong Khai, but the branch on MICHELIN's list is this Soi Nong Tao Lek one — don't go to the wrong spot. Dress is casual, and it makes a great late-morning meal before heading out to Nong Prajak Lake or north toward Nong Khai. Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Free-range duck noodles stewed 8–10 hours in a master stock kept simmering since the founder's father's era
mustOrder: Stewed duck noodles (choice of neck, wing, or thigh)
Stewed duck over rice served with soft blood
blocks.bestFor: A light-budget breakfast-lunch spot for anyone tracing Udon's MICHELIN trail and genuine duck noodle fans
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Peng Duck Noodles official Facebook page

blocks.name: Plaew
blocks.descHtml:
The budget is very light — tom yum pork noodles run 60 baht a bowl, seafood tom yum with jumbo prawns runs 65 baht, and you can eat well for under a hundred baht a head, making it one of the cheapest MICHELIN listings (Bib Gourmand 2024–2026) on the list. No bookings taken since it's a small shophouse noodle shop — just walk in and sit down. There's a shop phone, 034-267-325, to check before you head out.

The thing people miss most often is the hours — the shop only sells in the afternoon, roughly 11:30–16:30 (some 2025 sources say it opens at noon), and it can sell out before closing. Weekends bring long queues since earning the MICHELIN badge, so aim to arrive right at opening, 11:30–12:00. The shop sits in the city of Nakhon Pathom, Soi 5, Mu 1, near Phra Pathom Chedi, close to the waterworks junction. There's no train line to it — you'll need to drive or take a van/train into Nakhon Pathom town. Watch out for confusion with the Bangkok branches (Huai Khwang, Thewet) — the MICHELIN-awarded shop is only the original Nakhon Pathom location. Read the full review →
blocks.area: Mueang Nakhon Pathom (Soi 5 Mu 1, Phra Pathom Chedi area, near the waterworks junction)
blocks.signature: Old-recipe tom yum pork noodles with homemade bouncy pork balls
mustOrder: Old-recipe tom yum pork noodles (dry/soup) THB 60
Seafood tom yum with jumbo prawns/squid THB 65
Fish cakes with crispy fried basil
blocks.stayLabel: Hotels in prime spots in Bangkok
blocks.bestFor: Budget MICHELIN-hunters on a Nakhon Pathom day trip pairing a meal with a visit to Phra Pathom Chedi
blocks.zone: Mueang Nakhon Pathom (Soi 5 Mu 1, Phra Pathom Chedi area, near the waterworks junction)

blocks.text: Filter every Michelin restaurant in Thailand
blocks.label: Open the Michelin Finder

faq.q: Which Michelin noodle shop should I try first
faq.a: For a proper northern bowl, go to Khao Soi Mae Sai in Chiang Mai, where the chicken khao soi has a rich, spice-heavy broth made from scratch and starts at 55 baht. For beef lovers, Ten Suns in Bangkok braises cheek, tongue and tendon in a soft, fragrant stock the way a 60-year-old shop does. Both are worth pinning before anything else.

faq.q: Which bowl is the cheapest here
faq.a: Pa Lek Boat Noodles in Ayutthaya serves pork nam tok boat noodles with a secret-recipe broth for only tens of baht a bowl, so you can happily order several. Next in line is the chicken khao soi at Khao Soi Mae Sai, starting at 55 baht.

faq.q: What is the one dish I should not miss
faq.a: The tom yum pak mor egg noodles at Khun Jaeng in Khon Kaen, soft steamed rice sheets dropped into tom yum broth with a cracked egg, is a bowl Michelin flags as a must-try. Another is the giant river prawn pad thai at Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu, fried over high heat for that wok aroma and topped with salmon roe.

faq.q: Which one is worth splurging on
faq.a: Pad Thai Fai Ta Lu (Phra Nakhon) plates a giant river prawn pad thai at 599 baht, the priciest bowl in the group but worth it for the prawn. No Name Noodle in Bangkok is the other one to line up for, a clear shio soba built from over 30 ingredients, so arrive before it opens.

faq.q: Where do I go for noodles I can't easily find elsewhere
faq.a: Peng Duck Noodles in Udon Thani braises free-range duck for 8 to 10 hours in a master stock that has been simmering since the founder's day, and Guay Jub Chang Moi in Chiang Mai pairs a spiced rolled-noodle broth with crispy pork it marinates and fries over four hours. Both are flavors worth traveling to their home turf for.
